 Palace: ASEAN Summit clearing ops part of security measures
 by 
 Ruth Abbey Carlos
 Nov 10, 2026
 2:49 PM GMT+8
 SECURITY PREPS. Palace Press Officer Claire Castro defends the clearing operations near key venues of the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit and Related Summits during a press briefing on Tuesday (Nov. 10, 2026). Castro said the operations are part of security preparations to ensure the safety of visiting heads of state and foreign delegates ahead of the Philippines’ hosting of the regional gathering on Nov. 15–17. (PNA photo by Ruth Abbey Gita-Carlos) 
 MANILA – Malacañang on Tuesday defended the clearing operations around key venues of the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit and Related Summits, saying these form part of security preparations for the arrival of foreign leaders and dignitaries.
 In a press briefing, Palace Press Officer Claire Castro said the preparations aim to ensure the safety and security of nearly 20 heads of state and foreign delegates, while demonstrating the Philippines' capability to host major international events.
 "Ang Pangulo at ang administrasyon ay focus kung paano masasaayos at makukumpleto ang preparasyon na ito. Hindi lang para sa Pilipino kung hindi para ipakita sa buong mundo kung gaano kaprepara ang Pilipinas sa pagho-host ng ASEAN Summit (The President and the administration are focused on ensuring that these preparations are properly carried out and completed, not only for the Filipino people but also to show the world how prepared the Philippines is to host the ASEAN Summit)," Castro said.
 "Malaking bagay po na maipakita natin na tayo ay isang bansa na makapagbibigay ng sapat na seguridad sa mga liderato na pupunta sa ating bansa (It is important for us to demonstrate that the Philippines can provide adequate security for the leaders visiting our country).”
 Castro made the statement after ACT Teachers party-list Rep. Antonio Tinio criticized the Marcos administration for conducting clearing operations in Metro Manila ahead of the regional summit.
 Tinio accused the government of displacing street vendors, homeless individuals, and small business owners along major summit routes in Pasay City and Manila to "whitewash" the metropolis for the ASEAN gathering.
 Castro clarified that the clearing operations are not merely beautification efforts, noting that the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) continues to carry out regular cleaning activities.
 "Ang MMDA, alam naman natin, Metro Manila ang pinag-uusapan natin, hindi naman sila tumitigil sa paglilinis ng ating mga lugar. At ang kalinisan ng ating lugar hindi lang gobyerno ang nagsasagawa kundi buong taumbayan (As we know, the MMDA continuously cleans public areas across Metro Manila. Keeping our surroundings clean is not solely the government's responsibility but also of the public)," she said.
 She added the government wants to demonstrate the country's ability to ensure adequate security while showcasing the hospitality for which Filipinos are known.
 Castro also urged the public to focus on the positive impact of hosting the regional summit instead of politicizing the preparations.
 Meanwhile, Castro said the government would address possible disruptions, including those affecting public transportation, amid the planned two-day transport strike by transport group PISTON starting Nov. 16.
 She also appealed to groups planning demonstrations to avoid staging protests during the arrival of foreign delegates.
 "Kung anuman iyong maaapektuhan, kung may kinakailangan po na transportasyon na maaapektuhan noong gagawing pagra-rally, ito po ay tutugunan ng ating gobyerno (Whatever may be affected, including public transportation, by the planned rallies will be addressed by the government)," the Palace official said.
 "Ang hiling lang naman, kayo ay may panahon, marami kayong panahon kung anong gusto ninyong sabihin sa gobyerno mas maganda po sana kung hindi itapat ito sa pagdating ng ating mga bisita. Ipakita natin ang tunay na kagandahang ugali ng mga Pilipino (Our only request is for you to consider that you have plenty of time to air your concerns to the government. It would be better not to schedule the rallies during the arrival of our guests. Let us show the genuine hospitality and good character of the Filipino people).” (PNA)
